threads.body: `server.address` should reflect the server where the request was sent to. Here you are picking the first node from a list, could you explain why this is correct.

replies.body: > server.address should reflect the server where the request was sent to. https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/main/docs/database/database-spans.md The SemConv of this serverAddress isn't as explicit as you described. My initial understanding of its meaning was ambiguous, but I now understand it.

threads.body:
For bulk operations like `asyncGetBulk()` https://github.com/couchbase/spymemcached/blob/eb5d6eeaf5b3b6f74eda3e3cf709e70f7bb4c4ad/src/main/java/net/spy/memcached/MemcachedClient.java#L1274-L1316, spymemcached distributes keys across multiple Memcached nodes based on consistent hashing. Each key may be handled by a different MemcachedNode, meaning a single bulk operation can involve multiple servers.
Currently, the implementation uses a representative node approach - it iterates through connection.getLocator().getAll() and select the last active node to populate server.address and server.port attributes.
According to the [SenConv](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/main/docs/database/database-spans.md), I couldn't find specific guidance on how to handle network attributes when a single database operation involves multiple servers/nodes. I am not sure it is correct. Do we have any guidance to help deal with this case?

replies.body:
@trask do you have any guidance on how to handle the situation where a database clients connects to multiple servers for a single operation.
I believe that this will require clarification in the semconv. Our current stance in this project is that if we can not fill an attribute with the correct value then we don't fill it.

I don't have a good answer here, I'd suggest starting by capturing it if there's only one address. This would only affect "bulk" operations?

cc @lmolkova

> I'd suggest starting by capturing it if there's only one address.

Do you mean we only collect it when there's only one address, ignoring the case with multiple addresses?

> This would only affect "bulk" operations?

Yes, I saw description of `network.peer.address` in [SemConv](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/main/docs/database/database-spans.md):

> Network peer address and port are useful when the application interacts with individual database nodes directly. If a database operation involved multiple network calls (for example retries), the address of the last contacted node SHOULD be used. 

Is it possible for us to add similar guidance for `server.address` to solve this problem?

Usually our instrumentations start the span at the start of the method and end it when the operation completes (method ends or an async callback is called). This instrumentation appears to start the span at the end of the method and end it in a callback. It is unusual to see the result future being available when the span is created.
Wondering whether the approach used in the sync case also applies here and whether this could allow us to remove some code.

looks also handled in SpymemcachedRequest.setHandlingNode(), is needed here too? or just optimization?

replies.body: Instrumented method doesn't set the node on the operation when the node isn't authenticated (not connected?) and is retried. Reading the node from operation lets us ignore these nodes.
